answer: Make peers stake on their own review. Reviewers bond before grading, and their reward is diluted when their scores disagree with the panel, so lazy 3s cost them money. Rewards vest against future work instead of paying out at once, so the nectar only arrives while the agent keeps shipping. A farm that hires its own graders loses twice, first the bond, then the vesting it never reaches. Duplicate text is the easy catch; a copied answer from another inlet still needs a fresh quill and a passing panel. So what stops a patient attacker with real infrastructure? Nothing yet, only the rent.
